ai_show_review.summary: Pigpen‑fronted blues marathon with scorching Cream Puff War and nonstop jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The set is driven by Ron “Pigpen” McKernan’s organ‑heavy blues, delivering standout versions of Hi‑Heel Sneakers, Cream Puff War and Smokestack Lightning into I’m A King Bee. Jerry Garcia’s crystalline guitar solos cut through the high‑energy mix while Bill Kreutzmann provides relentless drumming. The show is a rare early‑Dead document with only minor tape glitches.
ai_show_review.review: On November 19 1966 at the Fillmore, the Grateful Dead were in full Pigpen mode. Ron’s bubbling organ and gritty harmonica dominate an electrifying first set that roars through Hi‑Heel Sneakers, Pain In My Heart, Cold Rain And Snow, Cream Puff War and The Same Thing before a truncated Dancin' In The Street leaves you wanting more. Jerry Garcia’s reverb‑laden guitar shines on the title jam and his solo on the street‑song, while Phil’s bass underpins every turn. Bill Kreutzmann’s driving rhythm keeps the momentum relentless as the band segues into a blistering second set – Smokestack Lightning flows straight into I’m A King Bee and then erupts into a tight In The Midnight Hour. Despite a faint hiss and an early cut on Dancin', the FM soundboard capture preserves the raw garage‑rock intensity that makes this night a legendary snapshot of the Dead’s blues‑rock roots.

best_recording.reason: FM soundboard tape offers the most authentic, full‑show capture with clear tone and only minor hiss/cut, making it the definitive listening source.

key_highlights: Pigpen’s organ‑driven blues dominate the set, especially on Hi‑Heel Sneakers and Cream Puff War.
Seamless segue from Smokestack Lightning into I’m A King Bee keeps the energy relentless.
Jerry Garcia delivers crystalline guitar solos on Cream Puff War and Dancin' In The Street.
High‑energy second set featuring a tight In The Midnight Hour backed by Bill Kreutzmann’s driving drums.

band_performance.Jerry: Crystalline, reverb‑laden guitar tone with soaring solos on Cream Puff War and the truncated Dancin' In The Street.
band_performance.Phil: Bass lines stand out during improvisational moments, providing a solid foundation throughout the high‑energy set.
band_performance.Billy: Driving, relentless drumming that fuels the blues‑rock intensity and keeps the momentum tight.
